project: Distributor sales representative selecting roofing contractors to contact and tracking saved work.
409 recorded GAF listings: 176 residential + 233 commercial. ZIP 10013, radius 50 miles. Snapshot data, not live search.
Search/filter/sort, explain priority, save a company, update status, first-contact and follow-up queues.
Notes and AI insights. No login, CRM sync, outreach automation, or per-representative ownership.

stack: Current choice
Why it fits
Current cost / limitation
Alternative
Why the alternative is not used here
Next.js + React + TypeScript
File-based routes, shared components, typed REST callers.
Separate frontend build; generated types do not validate HTTP at runtime.
Vite React SPA
Reason for the original selection is unrecorded. A SPA could work; changing frameworks adds migration work without a new MVP capability.
Flask + Pydantic
Python services with explicit input/output schemas; thin blueprint handlers.
OpenAPI must be maintained separately.
FastAPI
Original rejection is unrecorded. Automatic OpenAPI is useful, but moving the existing Flask services/routes is not required for this MVP.
PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy 2
Foreign keys, transactions, JSONB breakdowns, partial unique indexes.
Requires a database service; PostgreSQL-specific types reduce portability.
SQLite / file-only storage
SQLite could suit one local user; the chosen SQL/constraint model supports concurrent writes. Files alone do not provide these relational guarantees.
REST + OpenAPI + generated TS client
Explicit resource contracts and compile-time caller checks.
Routes, schemas, YAML, and generated types must stay aligned.
GraphQL / handwritten fetch types
No requirement for client-selected graph traversal. Handwritten types add another manual contract that can drift.
Docker Compose
One local service definition; named database volume and service DNS.
Three containers and image builds add local overhead.
Host-installed processes / Kubernetes
Host processes require manual runtime/database setup. Kubernetes adds orchestration concerns without measured availability or scale requirements.

flow: Diagram
Path
Implementation
Why this boundary
Alternative / trade-off
Data ingestion
GAF browser collection → JSON → CLI validation/upsert → stored scores.
D1: one-time collection avoids a runtime dependency on blocked GAF scraping.
Live API/feed: better freshness, but approved access and refresh policy are not available in the current implementation.
Browser request
Typed client → same-origin /api/v1 → Next.js rewrite → Flask route → service/query → PostgreSQL.
D15: one browser origin avoids separate cross-origin configuration.
Direct browser-to-Flask calls: workable, but require explicit CORS and deployment-origin management.
Save/status mutation
Validate → service write → commit → response → reconcile UI.
Commit defines persisted truth; UI pending/error state is not persistence.
Optimistic UI alone cannot enforce identity or recover an ambiguous commit.
Service layout
Modular monolith: routes, services, queries, models.
Keeps HTTP, policy, and persistence responsibilities separate.
Microservices introduce distributed failures and deployment boundaries without a measured need.

Unique prospect_id; status and timestamps remain independent of source updates.

Why chosen
Alternative
Why deferred / production consequence
create_all + PostgreSQL startup lock
D5: migrations excluded; advisory transaction lock serializes worker table creation.
Alembic schema migrations
Explicitly excluded from MVP. create_all cannot upgrade existing columns; introduce migrations before data-preserving schema changes.
Directory filter in SQL; remaining saved-lead filtering/sorting in Python
D19: database limits the directory; bounded saved set keeps queue logic small.
All filtering/counting/pagination in SQL
More query work for the MVP; move it when measured row count/memory/latency justifies it.
Snapshot upsert, then rescore
Reimports update source columns and preserve representative work.
Single atomic ingest-and-score transaction / staged publication
Current helpers commit separately. A rescore failure can leave rows without scores; atomicity/recovery remains work.

Enforces one saved prospect and one non-null company key under competing writes.

A check can race. Shared/missing phone cases and unexpected IntegrityError handling still need coverage.
No queue, cache, or status history
No active slow provider path; no measured need or approved audit requirement.
Durable jobs, cache, event history
Adds recovery/invalidation/schema complexity. Introduce each only for a defined requirement.
